_comment: What's new cards. One key per kit version, one short line per highlight.
The installer draws a card for every version it crossed during an upgrade,
and `exakit whats-new [version]` reads the same lines. This file is the only
source: there is nothing else to keep in step.
Rules, enforced by tests/whats-new.sh so a bad line cannot reach a user:
- a line is at most 68 characters, or the card would truncate it to '...'
- at most 6 lines per version, or the card stops being skimmable
- a version key is a plain dotted number (0.2.0), because the installer
sorts them to decide which cards a jump like 0.1.0 -> 0.4.0 crosses
Write what the reader can now DO, not what changed in the code. A first
install shows no cards at all, so every line here is read by someone who
already had the kit working and wants to know what is different.
0.2.0: The installer downloads 4x less: 27 MB down to 6.5 MB.
Updates come from a published set of tested versions.
exakit status names any component that failed to install.
exakit version groups the kit, components and add-ons.
The marketplace shows add-ons you already have, and why.
Menus say what the keys actually do.
